newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters says emphatic no to capital gains tax.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters says emphatic no to capital gains tax.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters repeated on Thursday that the government had no intention to introduce a capital gains tax.
"I can say no, emphatically, this government has no plans to introduce a capital gains tax," Peters said in reply to a question in parliament.
"There are a number of significant problems with extending income tax to include all capital gains," he said.
Peters said he could understand Wednesday's comments by Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash in relation to Brash's concerns about inflation from the housing market.
"However, in this area it is worth emphasising the existing law with respect to people who trade in houses is that they are already liable to be taxed," Peters said.
He reiterated that the government was committed to further tax cuts if the fiscal position allowed.
